clue.text: Every day member gets censure in the liberal paper

parts.note: happening every day

indicators.note: the member and the censure are placed inside the word that follows
a liberal reading is a loose, free one, so the little word is taken freely and rearranged

parts.note: the word 'the' rearranged, opened up to take the next pieces between its E and H
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
a rap over the knuckles is a reprimand

explanation.surface: A daily reader is told off by a left-leaning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The member and the censure go inside the rearranged little word. The joke is that the Daily Telegraph is a famously conservative British broadsheet, hardly a liberal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Telegraph is a British national newspaper, an example of a paper.

clue.text: Alerted Todd, who's knocked unconscious

indicators.note: something knocked about is battered out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: all fourteen letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Todd was warned of danger yet still got knocked out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of who's is read as 'is', linking the jumbled letters to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead to the world is an idiom for sleeping deeply or being completely out cold.

clue.text: Burning oil in church nave's initially seen regularly

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of nave

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: first and third letters of seen

explanation.surface: Fragrant oil burns in a church, glimpsed now and then down the nave.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is an aromatic substance, often resin or scented oil, burned to give off fragrant smoke.

clue.text: Agreement on trade foundering one year previously

parts.note: yes expresses agreement

indicators.note: foundering means collapsing, so the letters of trade fall into a new order

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for one year

explanation.surface: A trade deal was agreed but collapsed a year ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday can mean in the recent past, formerly, as in yesterday's methods, so it stands for an earlier time.

clue.text: Veteran sneered at concealed climbing net

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, from bottom to top
the letters lie concealed inside the run of words before it

parts.note: found inside veteran sneered

explanation.surface: An old soldier scoffs at a camouflage net slung up a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch or trap it, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Beguile sweetheart bearing tea and books

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of sweet

parts.note: the central letter of sweet
a compass bearing such as north, N
char or cha is British slang for tea
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A lover wins someone over by bringing them tea and books.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or delight someone, a close synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Limitless dry period is hard

indicators.note: without its limits the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a drought is a long spell without rain

explanation.surface: An endless spell without rain is a hard time for farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough can mean harsh or difficult, as in having a rough time.

clue.text: Playwright's retaining right for publisher

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the writer's name holds a letter within it

parts.note: Harold Pinter, the English dramatist
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dramatist keeps the rights to his work when dealing with a publishing house.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer produces and issues printed material, and historically printers were the publishers of books.

clue.text: Tourist attraction provided by resort's drag queen?

parts.note: Blackpool is a seaside resort in Lancashire, northern England
to drag is to tow, so one who drags would be a tower

explanation.surface: A seaside town's star drag act draws in the visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a drag queen is not a performer here but one who drags, a TOWER. Blackpool Tower is the resort's famous Eiffel-style landmark, home to a ballroom and circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blackpool Tower is a landmark visited by millions of holidaymakers, an example of a sightseeing draw.

clue.text: Denounces experts securing Cuba-America meeting

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the experts hold other pieces inside

parts.note: aces are experts at something

indicators.note: the two country abbreviations meet, joined side by side

parts.note: C is Cuba's international vehicle registration code
the United States

explanation.surface: Specialists condemn a summit between Cuba and the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to publicly charge or condemn them, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Essential to have key Russian top level domain and agents on line

parts.note: C is a musical key
.ru ends Russian web addresses
the Central Intelligence Agency
L for line, placed after the agents

explanation.surface: Online security needs a key, a Russian web domain and agents on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On line' looks like online, the internet, but it only puts L, for line, after the agents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial is vitally important, decisive, so essential is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Trace some incriminating evidence

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A detective finds a little bit of damning evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight amount or hint of a colour or quality, much like a trace.

clue.text: One's very sad and listless

parts.note: a means one; the 's is read as 'is'
pitiably sad, arousing pity

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply unhappy and lacking all energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apathetic means showing no interest or enthusiasm, which matches lacking energy and spirit.

clue.text: Red tent is possibly the most groovy

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of the letters

parts.note: seven letters
two more letters

explanation.surface: A red tent might be the coolest thing at the festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'is' is fodder; the second is the link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Groovy is dated slang for fashionable, so the superlative matches the most fashionable.

clue.text: Small outing to get team kit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: A little excursion to pick up the club uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a sports team's strip is its playing kit, shirts and shorts in club colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side's colours are called its strip, the clothing the players wear.

clue.text: Hot into retail angle with oysters, maybe

indicators.note: into means going inside the word that follows

parts.note: to retail goods is to sell them
H for hot, as on taps
to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: A fishmonger gets keen on selling oysters, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' looks like a geometric corner but is the verb to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are bivalve molluscs eaten as seafood, an example of the category; the maybe signals an example.

clue.text: Opponent of energy with which young chaps go west

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means travelling right to left

parts.note: Y for young, as in YMCA
chaps are men

explanation.surface: An adversary of energetic young men heading off to the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is someone hostile who fights against you, an adversary or foe.

clue.text: Country seat's ruined, bringing in zero tax

indicators.note: bringing in means taking other pieces inside
something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: these four letters rearranged
O looks like zero
NI is National Insurance, a UK payroll tax

explanation.surface: A country house is in ruins after paying no tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country seat' reads as a stately home, but country alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation in northern Europe, an example of a country.

clue.text: Padre does reform outlaw

indicators.note: to re-form is to shape again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nine letters

explanation.surface: A priest sets about reforming a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' looks like moral improvement by the padre, but it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit of the Wild West kind, a criminal on the run.

clue.text: End wild chaos and peter out

indicators.note: chaos is total disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: seven letters

explanation.surface: Stop the wild chaos and let it fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to diminish gradually until nothing is left, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Admit jury using bad language's no good

definitions.note: the definition is the verb together with its typical object

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: cursing
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A juror's foul language means they are no good for the jury.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after language reads as 'is', and 'no good' removes G from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurors are sworn in by taking an oath, which admits them formally to serve on the jury.

clue.text: Kind of maths requiring a large brain's not popular

parts.note: taken as written
LGE is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is removed

parts.note: the organ of thought; 's reads as 'is'
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A branch of mathematics that needs a big brain is unpopular.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics using letters for unknown quantities.

clue.text: Ordnance Survey copy is boxed to send to Coventry

parts.note: OS, Britain's mapping agency

indicators.note: something boxed is enclosed, so it goes inside the copy

parts.note: to trace a map is to copy it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A copied map from the national survey is packed off to Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them; Coventry is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean deliberately excluding someone from a group by shunning them socially.

clue.text: Look for a wife with top class sex appeal!

parts.note: taken as written
W for wife, as in genealogies
A is the top grade or class
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man seeks a partner who is first-rate and alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins A for top class on to the wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To look for something can mean to expect or anticipate it, which is to wait for it.

clue.text: Kindle's brilliant!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set burning, ignite

explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises a Kindle e-reader, but Kindle is the verb to set fire to.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means ignite, as with a fire; as an adjective it means bright and luminous.

clue.text: Left with an old length of cord

parts.note: a yard is an imperial length of three feet, now largely replaced by metric

explanation.surface: Someone left holding an old piece of string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'length of cord' reads as one phrase, but 'old length' is YARD and 'cord' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn round the neck to hold a badge, whistle or key.

clue.text: Meteorological effect from fresh air preceding northern front

indicators.note: preceding means the rearranged letters come before the rest
fresh means the letters of air are made anew in a different order

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: fresh air ahead of a northern front, with an optical effect to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' looks like a weather front, which fits the surface, but here it is the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is an arc of colours caused by sunlight refracting through raindrops, a weather phenomenon.

clue.text: Dream of rook in flight?

parts.note: the rook in chess is also called a castle
anything in flight is airborne

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of a crow flying overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook looks like the bird, which fits flight, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle in the air is an idiom for an unrealistic plan or daydream, a fanciful hope.
